questions.title: Simple Interest
statement: Read the principal amount, the yearly rate of interest and the time in years. Calculate the simple interest using SI = P × R × T / 100, and the total amount (P + SI).

questions.title: Duration Formatter
statement: Read a duration in seconds and print it as days and a clock time in `HH:MM:SS` format. Use `//` and `%` to split the seconds, and format each of hours, minutes and seconds with two digits (for example `05`).
questions.solution:
seconds = int(input())

days = seconds // 86400
remaining = seconds % 86400
hours = remaining // 3600
minutes = (remaining % 3600) // 60
secs = remaining % 60

print(f"{days} days {hours:02d}:{minutes:02d}:{secs:02d}")
print("Total minutes:", seconds // 60)

questions.title: Quadratic Equation Roots
statement: Read the coefficients `a`, `b` and `c` of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 and find the discriminant d = b² − 4ac.
Discriminant
Nature of roots
Real and distinct
Real and equal
Complex
Find the roots with (−b ± √d) / 2a, taking `+` for Root 1 and `−` for Root 2. Use `math.sqrt()` when d ≥ 0, and `cmath.sqrt()` when d < 0 (the roots are then complex numbers).
output: Lines 2 and 3: `Root 1: <r1>` and `Root 2: <r2>`. For real roots, print them rounded to 2 decimal places. For complex roots, print them as `<real>+<imag>j` or `<real>-<imag>j`, with both parts rounded to 2 decimal places (for example `-1.00+2.00j`)
samples:
Nature: Real and distinct
Root 1: 2.00
Root 2: 1.00
tests:
Nature: Real and equal
Root 1: -1.00
Root 2: -1.00

Nature: Real and distinct
Root 1: 2.00
Root 2: -2.00

Nature: Real and distinct
Root 1: 7.00
Root 2: 0.00
questions.solution:
import math
import cmath

a = int(input())
b = int(input())
c = int(input())

d = b * b - 4 * a * c

if d > 0:
    print("Nature: Real and distinct")
elif d == 0:
    print("Nature: Real and equal")
else:
    print("Nature: Complex")

if d >= 0:
    r1 = (-b + math.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    r2 = (-b - math.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    print(f"Root 1: {r1:.2f}")
    print(f"Root 2: {r2:.2f}")
else:
    r1 = (-b + cmath.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    r2 = (-b - cmath.sqrt(d)) / (2 * a)
    print(f"Root 1: {r1.real:.2f}{r1.imag:+.2f}j")
    print(f"Root 2: {r2.real:.2f}{r2.imag:+.2f}j")

statement: Read a sentence and print the number of words, the sentence with each word reversed (words stay in the same order), the sentence in title case (`str.title()`), and the longest word (the first one if there is a tie).
input: Line 1: a sentence of words separated by single spaces

questions.solution:

questions.title: Leap Year
statement: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 400, or if it is divisible by 4 but not by 100. Read a year and print whether it is a leap year, and how many days February has in that year.
output: Line 1: `Leap year` or `Not a leap year`
samples:
Not a leap year
February has 28 days
tests:
Not a leap year
February has 28 days

Not a leap year
February has 28 days
questions.solution:
year = int(input())

if year % 400 == 0 or (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0):
    print("Leap year")
    print("February has 29 days")
else:
    print("Not a leap year")
    print("February has 28 days")

questions.title: Day of the Week
statement: Read a day number from 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday). Use `match-case` to print the day's name. Use a combined pattern `case 6 | 7` (or similar) to decide whether it is a weekday or the weekend.
output: If the number is not 1 to 7, print only one line: `Invalid day`
questions.solution:
day = int(input())

match day:
    case 1:
        name = "Monday"
    case 2:
        name = "Tuesday"
    case 3:
        name = "Wednesday"
    case 4:
        name = "Thursday"
    case 5:
        name = "Friday"
    case 6:
        name = "Saturday"
    case 7:
        name = "Sunday"
    case _:
        name = None

if name is None:
    print("Invalid day")
else:
    print(name)
    match day:
        case 6 | 7:
            print("Weekend")
        case _:
            print("Weekday")

questions.title: Digit Operations
statement: Read a non-negative integer. Using a `while` loop with `%` and `//` (not string functions), find the sum of its digits, the number with its digits reversed, and how many digits it has.
samples:
Sum of digits: 15
Reversed: 54321
Digit count: 5

Sum of digits: 3
Reversed: 21
Digit count: 4
tests:
Sum of digits: 0
Reversed: 0
Digit count: 1

Sum of digits: 7
Reversed: 7
Digit count: 1

Sum of digits: 1
Reversed: 1
Digit count: 10

Sum of digits: 18
Reversed: 909
Digit count: 3
questions.solution:
n = int(input())

total = 0
reverse = 0
count = 0
temp = n
while True:
    digit = temp % 10
    total += digit
    reverse = reverse * 10 + digit
    count += 1
    temp //= 10
    if temp == 0:
        break

print("Sum of digits:", total)
print("Reversed:", reverse)
print("Digit count:", count)

questions.title: GCD and LCM
statement: Read two positive integers. Find their GCD using Euclid's method with a `while` loop: repeatedly replace (a, b) with (b, a % b) until b becomes 0; then a is the GCD. The LCM is a × b ÷ GCD. Two numbers are co-prime if their GCD is 1.
questions.solution:
a = int(input())
b = int(input())

x, y = a, b
while y != 0:
    x, y = y, x % y

gcd = x
lcm = a * b // gcd

print("GCD:", gcd)
print("LCM:", lcm)
print("Co-prime:", "Yes" if gcd == 1 else "No")

questions.title: Second Largest
statement: Read a list of integers and print the largest value and the second largest distinct value. If all values are the same, there is no second largest; print `None`.
questions.solution:
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

largest = max(numbers)
others = [n for n in numbers if n != largest]

questions.title: Rotate a List
statement: Read a list of integers and a number `k`. Rotate the list to the left by `k` positions using slicing. If `k` is larger than the list length, use `k % length`. Then print the first and last elements of the rotated list as a tuple.
questions.solution:
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
k = int(input())

k = k % len(numbers)
rotated = numbers[k:] + numbers[:k]

print("Rotated:", rotated)

questions.title: Rank List
statement: Read `n` students with their marks and store each as a tuple `(name, marks)` in a list. Sort the list by marks from highest to lowest; students with equal marks are sorted by name alphabetically. Use `sorted()` with a `lambda` key.
Print the rank list, then print the top student's tuple.
questions.solution:
n = int(input())

students = []
for _ in range(n):
    name, marks = input().split()
    students.append((name, int(marks)))

ranked = sorted(students, key=lambda s: (-s[1], s[0]))

for rank, (name, marks) in enumerate(ranked, start=1):
    print(f"{rank}. {name} - {marks}")
print("Top:", ranked[0])

questions.title: Two List Comparison
statement: Read two lists of integers. First remove duplicates from the first list while keeping the original order (use a set to remember what you have already seen). Then use set operations to compare the two lists.
samples:

Common: [2, 3]
Union: [1, 2, 3, 5]
Only in first: [1]

Without duplicates: [1, 2, 3]
Common: []
Union: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
Only in first: [1, 2, 3]
tests:

Common: [7]
Union: [7]
Only in first: []

Without duplicates: [5]
Common: [5]
Union: [5, 6]
Only in first: []

Without duplicates: [-1, 0, 1]

questions.solution:
first = list(map(int, input().split()))
second = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = set()
unique = []
for n in first:
    if n not in seen:
        seen.add(n)
        unique.append(n)

a = set(first)
b = set(second)

print("Without duplicates:", unique)
print("Common:", sorted(a & b))
print("Union:", sorted(a | b))
print("Only in first:", sorted(a - b))

questions.title: Factorial and Combinations
statement: Write a function `factorial(n)` that uses a loop to return n!. Then use it to find nCr = n! / (r! × (n − r)!).
questions.solution:
def factorial(n):
    result = 1
    for i in range(2, n + 1):
        result *= i
    return result


n = int(input())
r = int(input())

ncr = factorial(n) // (factorial(r) * factorial(n - r))
print(f"{n}! = {factorial(n)}")
print(f"{n}C{r} = {ncr}")

Line

questions.solution:

questions.title: Matrix Transpose
statement: Read a matrix with `r` rows and `c` columns. Use a nested list comprehension to build its transpose (rows become columns). Also use list comprehensions to find the sum of each row and of each column of the original matrix.
input: Next `r` lines: `c` integers separated by spaces
output: `c` lines: the rows of the transpose, numbers separated by single spaces
questions.solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
matrix = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]

transpose = [[matrix[i][j] for i in range(r)] for j in range(c)]
row_sums = [sum(row) for row in matrix]
col_sums = [sum(matrix[i][j] for i in range(r)) for j in range(c)]

for row in transpose:
    print(*row)
print("Row sums:", row_sums)
print("Column sums:", col_sums)

questions.title: File Word Count
statement: Read `n` lines of text and write them to a file named `notes.txt`. Then open the file again in read mode and count its lines, words and characters (not counting the newline at the end of each line). Also print the longest line (the first one if there is a tie). Use `with open(...)` for both steps.
samples:
3
Python is easy
Files store data
Practice daily

Words: 8
Characters: 44
Longest line: Files store data

Lines: 1
Words: 1
Characters: 5
Longest line: Hello
tests:
Lines: 2
Words: 4
Characters: 10
Longest line: a b c

4
one
two words
three more words
four

Lines: 4
Words: 7
Characters: 32
Longest line: three more words
questions.solution:
n = int(input())
with open("notes.txt", "w") as file:
    for _ in range(n):
        file.write(input() + "\n")

lines = words = chars = 0
longest = ""
with open("notes.txt", "r") as file:
    for line in file:
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        lines += 1
        words += len(line.split())
        chars += len(line)
        if len(line) > len(longest):
            longest = line

print("Lines:", lines)
print("Words:", words)
print("Characters:", chars)
print("Longest line:", longest)
